To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed and evaluated a new family of graph neural network-based transformations of graph-structured data, where all predictions can easily be explained as logical inferences, and where such explanations can be automatically extracted.

(a) we introduce MGNNs, a new class of GNNs that can be explained as logical rules in Datalog and can be trained effectively; (b) we show how to automatically extract the rules from any MGNN and use them to explain its predictions; and (c) we show how our MGNNs can be used to solve knowledge graph completion problems.
We present a novel framework that enables GNN-based models to be trained on knowledge graphs and to produce explainable predictions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following research question: can we design GNN-based architectures that can be explained as logical inferences?
the design of a new family of neural network architectures, called monotonic graph neural networks (MGNNs).

the authors propose a method to train GNNs that can explain their predictions.
the proposed approach is able to provide a novel and effective way of learning symbolic explanations for GNN-based models over knowledge graphs.
the proposed approach provides a new way to train GNNs that can be applied to knowledge graphs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed an approach that can learn effective GNN-based models that can explain their predictions in terms of a Datalog program.
we propose a novel approach to explain GNN-based models over knowledge graphs.
we propose a new family (MGNN) of graph neural networks, which are monotonic and can be used for knowledge graph reasoning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GNN-based models can be used for tasks that require symbolic explanations, such as knowledge graph completion, while retaining the ability to learn complex transformations of data.
, by using MGNNs, we can obtain models that are as accurate as state-of-the-art GNNs, while also providing symbolic, explainable predictions.
GNNs are a powerful tool that can be used to train models that are not only effective but also interpretable.
